claims.text: LeetCode 516 asks for the length of the longest palindromic subsequence; a subsequence preserves relative order while allowing deletions. The official constraints are length 1..1000 over lowercase English letters, with examples bbbab -> 4 and cbbd -> 2.

The candidate's interval-DP implementation uses dp[i][j] for the longest palindromic-subsequence length in s[i..j], handles matching and nonmatching endpoints with the stated recurrence, and matches an independent brute-force subsequence oracle for all 9,841 strings over {a,b,c} of lengths 0..8 in addition to the official examples and explicit boundaries.

The implementation fills O(n^2) interval states with O(1) work per state and stores an n-by-n integer table, supporting O(n^2) time and O(n^2) auxiliary-space claims. The repository-local null/empty handling is explicitly separated from the official LeetCode input contract.

checks: all 9,841 strings over alphabet {a,b,c} of lengths 0..8 against an independent brute-force subsequence oracle

findings: All three source variants are covered by the same LeetCode 516 coding answer.
The candidate matches the official problem contract, constraints, and examples.
The interval-DP explanation, fill order, Java implementation, and complexity claims are mutually consistent.
The reproducible validation compares against an independent brute-force oracle over 9,841 generated short strings, not just examples.
Follow-ups are specific to the problem and include recurrence, reconstruction, memory compression, and alternative LCS framing.
The project-experience section explicitly avoids fabricating production or interview experience.
